analysis.title: "Underweight Is Overcrowded": Goldman's Garrett Says 'FOBU' Means The Next Premium Dollar Chases Calls, Not Puts
key_insights: Goldman's Brian Garrett says the S&P 500 made a new all-time high on Tuesday (Oct 6) but the breakout faded by week's end. Index implied vols closed near 5-year lows, with QQQ standing out. He describes 'fear of benchmark underperformance' (FOBU) as driving the chase.

The S&P broke through the 7,800 gamma wall on Tuesday. The first 90 minutes after the open were 'categorically the busiest we've been in months' with bullish activity: spot up, vol up, with short-dated implieds higher.

Garrett lists five drivers of the Tuesday move: higher realized vol, significant call demand, underweight index exposure, clean gamma positioning, and the realization that only 57 sessions remain in the year and 'underweight' is crowded.

SPX 1-month 25-delta call implied vol was higher with spot near 7,900 than with spot back at 7,800 later in the week. The one-week realized correlation between the S&P and its 1-month 25-delta call vol, normally near -1, flipped to roughly +0.5. This is read as forced buying rather than an 'economy is fine' bid.

Prime Services data: gross exposure rose 3.8 points on the week (53rd percentile over 1 year, 80th over 3 years). Net exposure rose 0.5 points to 46.9, which is the 2nd percentile over 1 year and 4th over 3 years. The long/short ratio fell to a 1-year low and sits in the 1st percentile over 5 years.

Hedge funds have added positions but little direction, and what direction they have is concentrated in a small number of stocks. CTAs hold roughly $40B of US equities while European exposure has fallen to barely above $10B.

Goldman's cash desk flagged Thursday afternoon as the most interesting flow of the week. A headline on AI model revenues 'brought out significant semis and tech supply', which Garrett reads as 'nervous / forced length in the space'.

Non-AI stocks keep getting sold. Russell futures positioning is at a record short and IWM short interest is at a record high, while the cost of a 1-month 5% OTM IWM call sits near the bottom of its range.

Garrett says 2026 'will likely go down as the most dispersive calendar year in history'. The gap between average-stock realized vol and index realized vol was 27 over the three months to Oct 8 and 24 over nine months.

VIX upside convexity 'has gone extremely bid' while SPX downside convexity 'remains extremely offered'. VIX 1-month call skew is near the top of its range and SPX 1-month put skew is at the bottom. An index vol desk colleague says 'it feels like there is a higher probability of VIX >25 than there is of SPX -2%'.
Goldman sees two resolutions to the skew mismatch: 'either we get a correlated correction (VIX spike) or we drift (SPX puts decay away)'.
Goldman's conclusion is that 'there is accelerant under the hood' and that 'the marginal premium dollar feels increasingly likely to chase upside through calls than protect downside through puts'.
QQQ call vol relative to the S&P nearly doubled over the summer and has retraced to its long-run average, so upside is no longer priced for an AI mania.

The index desk says the October 30 expiry 'stands out' because it captures the Fed, economic data and roughly 65% of S&P market cap reporting, without paying up for the midterms. A call struck 2.5% above spot expiring Oct 30 costs 19bps on SPY, 58bps on QQQ and 62bps on IWM.
IWM vol is below its 10th percentile, so for those unwilling to cover Russell shorts outright, an upside IWM call does the job of a synthetic put on the short.

Banks into earnings: XLF is 6.5% off its highs with the S&P at records, yet implied earnings moves do not reflect it. The ratio of recent drawdown to earnings straddle is about 5x, which Goldman reads as 'implied move cheap'. The desk expects trading activity and the AI funding calendar to be the most debated topics.

Goldman's desk pitches year-end outperformance options: S&P ex-AI over the S&P (2.5% OTM for 2.75%) and equal-weight RSP over the S&P (2.5% OTM for 1.75%). These pay on relative performance, so they can work even in a down market (S&P -10% with RSP -3% is 700bps of outperformance).

New pair: long defense (ITA, down 20% from August highs) against industrials ex-defense (XLI, down 9%). Garrett frames it as government-backed demand versus the part of the market that is 'prisoner to rates and the cycle'.
Biotech: the eight-week gross-down is 'almost without precedent' and looks like an opportunity to the desk. Utilities rose 4% last week but remain well off highs, with the Street 'max short gamma'.

Power: the desk calls power the most underappreciated AI bottleneck and favors its Power Up America basket. It argues positioning is low, valuation has normalized, and earnings revisions should rise as independent power producers sign long-term deals with mega-cap tech.

Caution from the note: last quarter was the most volatile in a decade for the Mag 7 (11% average realized move). Across the index, beats were rewarded with 35bps of next-day outperformance versus 95bps historically, one of the narrowest payoffs on record.

Zero Hedge's own view: nothing in the note says rates, credit, oil or the consumer improved, and September payrolls printed 29K, below all estimates. It suggests a FOBU-driven melt-up into Oct 30 followed by the event the VIX calls were bought for, and plans to check back after Oct 30.

tension_points.theme: VIX calls versus SPX puts skew
tension_points.bull_case: Drift: SPX puts decay away while the marginal premium dollar chases upside calls, and underexposed funds are forced to buy as the market grinds higher.
tension_points.bear_case: A correlated correction with a VIX spike. VIX upside convexity is extremely bid while SPX downside convexity is extremely offered, and Zero Hedge notes the longs concentrated in AI have itchy trigger ffingers.

tension_points.bull_case: Net exposure in the 2nd percentile, record-short small caps, clean gamma and cheap upside mean a FOBU-driven chase can run for a couple of weeks if the S&P clears Tuesday's high on decent bank prints.
tension_points.bear_case: Nothing in the note shows rates, credit, oil or the consumer improving, payrolls printed 29K, and earnings beats are rewarded with only 35bps versus 95bps historically.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The S&P failing to get back through Tuesday's all-time high on bank earnings.
